A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SupportNet/KeyNet research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original retrieval, cluster-routing, timing, training-dynamics, and noisy-query experiments in Section 4 and Appendix A.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds larger-scale retrieval, additional indexing backends, encoder experiments, ablations, and distributional analyses.

M1.justification: The SupportNet and KeyNet architectures, homogenization wrapper, losses, query augmentation, clustered formulation, and inference procedures remain substantively unchanged. Additional backends and configurations evaluate the existing method.

E1.justification: V2 retains the four original BEIR datasets and adds biomedical retrieval on BioASQ, with approximately 15 million keys (Appendix A.9, Figure 28). This extends evaluation to a new domain and substantially larger database.

E2.justification: Beyond the retained centroid-routing and FAISS-IVF comparisons, v2 evaluates original-query ScaNN, SOAR, and LeanVec against their KeyNet-mapped counterparts (Figures 19–27). ScaNN's underlying work was cited in v1, but these comparisons were absent.

E3.justification: V2 adds retrieval-latency and search-budget reporting alongside FLOPs, a 128-cluster routing experiment, and 768-dimensional MPNet/DistilRoBERTa configurations. It also introduces controlled loss-weight and 1/3/5/7-billion-sample training-horizon experiments. The original 1,000-vector validation protocol remains.

E4.justification: New analyses isolate loss components, examine training-horizon saturation, test encoder sensitivity and larger cluster counts, and characterize query/key distributions (Appendices A.5–A.7 and A.10). Noise robustness reporting expands to NQ/Quora FLOPs and latency plots; the original capacity and training-dynamics analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix A.10 adds kernel-density estimation and empirical mean/median summaries for distributional characterization. This expands descriptive statistical reporting, while Table 1's averaging over 100 timing runs is unchanged. No new seed-variability reporting, confidence intervals, or significance tests appear.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial routing, backend, latency, encoder, BioASQ, ablation, and distributional results. For example, Figure 15 reports relative transport error declining from approximately 0.40 at 1B training samples to 0.365 at 7B. These are new experimental conditions; the original timing table and several relocated plots retain their results.

T1.justification: The support-function formulation, homogeneity construction, Euler-based loss motivation, network-sizing derivation, and relative transport-error definition remain equivalent. V2 adds explanations but no substantive theorem, proof, formal assumption, or mathematical correction.

C1.justification: The core amortized-MIPS contribution remains, but v2 broadens its principal empirical claims. The abstract and conclusion now assert benefits under latency and probe budgets, across indexing backends and encoder families, under moderate query shift, and at scales up to 15M keys.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations linking query/key mismatch to retrieval headroom, distinguishes model-size preferences under FLOPs versus latency, and interprets loss and training-horizon tradeoffs. It also discusses KeyNet's output-size limitation at high cluster counts and backend-dependent saturation, substantially expanding applicability analysis.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-access link in the abstract, discloses typical training volumes of 1–10B samples, and specifies configurations for the new experiments and distributional analyses. Most existing preprocessing, optimizer, loss-weight, and EMA details remain unchanged; the linked resource was not accessed.

R1.justification: V2 adds references on amortized optimization, learned/query-aware indices, additional backends, and BioASQ. It refines v1's blanket characterization of prior indices as query-agnostic by acknowledging approaches that use query statistics during construction, while retaining the central research positioning.

P1.justification: The overall main-section structure and most method prose remain. V2 rewrites the abstract, conclusion, and selected experimental passages, moves the MRR/transport tradeoff discussion to Appendix A.4, promotes robustness into the main text, and adds an author contribution statement.

P2.justification: V2 adds a deployment schematic and new routing, ablation, scaling, and distribution figures. Retrieval displays expand into grids covering FLOPs, search budget, and latency; existing plots are relocated or reformatted, and Table 1 receives a revised layout while retaining its values.

improvement.justification: Added ablations, larger-cluster tests, and multi-backend latency comparisons make training choices and deployment limits more assessable than v1's largely FAISS/FLOPs-based validation. The net gain is limited by reporting inconsistencies: Figures 12–13 repeat identical curves under NQ/Quora labels, Appendix A.9 discusses BioASQ S/M results absent from Figure 28, and broad dominance claims exceed the SOAR FLOPs evidence.
